# Florence 1347 – Metallurgy & materials

- **Copper smelting and bronze** [`copper_bronze`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/copper_bronze.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Founders cast bells and, since 1326, a few small cannon. For Andrea Pisano's Baptistery doors (1330s) Venetian founders were brought in. Tin comes from Cornwall. Local: bell founders; Baptistery south doors (Andrea Pisano, cast 1330–36); copper and silver mines of Massa Marittima. Elsewhere: Venice, bronze founders.
- **Bloomery iron (wrought iron, forging, carburising)** [`bloomery_iron`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/bloomery_iron.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Elba ore, under Pisan control, is smelted with charcoal in water-powered ironworks on the Maremma coast and in the Pistoia hills. Local: Elba (Rio mines); ironworks of the Maremma and Pistoia mountains; Arte dei Fabbri.
- **Hardening and tempering steel** [`steel_heat_treatment`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/steel_heat_treatment.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Armourers and cutlers harden and temper by colour and by secret quenching recipes (urine, radish juice). That carbon makes steel is unknown. Local: Arte dei Corazzai e Spadai (armourers and swordsmiths). Elsewhere: Milan, the leading armourers.
- **Cementation (blister) steel and case hardening** [`cementation_steel`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/cementation_steel.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept high. Smiths case-harden files and tools in charcoal, horn and salt. Converting whole bars in sealed chests is not done; good steel is bought from Lombardy. Elsewhere: Brescia and Bergamo valleys, natural steel; Styria.
- **Blast furnace and cast iron** [`blast_furnace_cast_iron`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/blast_furnace_cast_iron.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept medium. Iron that runs liquid is a spoiled smelt to a Tuscan ironmaster. It needs a taller shaft, stronger water-driven bellows and a use for the brittle metal. Elsewhere: Sweden (Lapphyttan) and the Mark in Westphalia, early blast furnaces; China, cast iron for eighteen centuries.
- **Smelting iron with coke** [`coke_iron`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/coke_iron.md) — K0, use none, make impossible, accept medium. No blast furnace and no coking coal in Tuscany; ironworks run on charcoal. Elsewhere: China, coal in iron smelting since the 11th c..
- **Puddling and rolling (wrought iron from pig iron with coal)** [`puddling_wrought_iron`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/puddling_wrought_iron.md) — K0, use none, make impossible, accept medium. There is no pig iron to convert; the bloomery makes wrought iron directly.
- **Crucible steel (wootz, Huntsman's cast steel)** [`crucible_steel`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/crucible_steel.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept high. Watered 'Damascus' blades reach Italy through Venice and are admired; how they are made is a mystery. Local crucibles and furnaces fail below the heat needed. Elsewhere: India and Persia, crucible steel ingots.

- **Alloy, tool and stainless steels** [`alloy_stainless_steel`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/alloy_stainless_steel.md) — K0, use none, make impossible, accept medium. Chromium, nickel, tungsten and manganese are unknown as metals.
- **Refractories (fireclay, crucibles, furnace linings)** [`refractories_fireclay`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/refractories_fireclay.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept high. Glassmakers and goldsmiths make their own pots and crucibles from selected clays; these limit furnace heat. Finding a good fireclay is a prospecting job. Local: glass furnaces of the Valdelsa; potters of Impruneta and Montelupo.
- **Brass and metallic zinc** [`zinc_brass`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/zinc_brass.md) — K3, use partial, make hard, accept high. Brass is made by heating copper with calamine and mostly imported as sheet, wire and basins. Nobody knows calamine holds a metal; zinc boils away unless condensed. Elsewhere: Dinant and the Meuse valley, brass goods; Zawar in India, metallic zinc.
- **Cupellation, parting and assaying of silver and gold** [`cupellation_assaying`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/cupellation_assaying.md) — K3, use correct, make easy, accept high. The mint guards the florin's fineness by touchstone, cupellation and salt cementation; Pegolotti's handbook gives the recipes. The most quantitative craft in the city. Local: Zecca (mint); goldsmiths, members of the Arte di Por Santa Maria; silver-lead mines of the Colline Metallifere.
- **Mercury and amalgamation of gold and silver** [`mercury_amalgam`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/mercury_amalgam.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Goldsmiths fire-gild with gold amalgam and breathe the fumes. Mercury is not used to win silver from ore. Quicksilver ointments treat skin diseases and lice. Local: goldsmiths and gilders; apothecaries (mercury); cinnabar of Monte Amiata. Elsewhere: Almadén (Spain).
- **Lead is a cumulative poison** [`lead_hazard`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/lead_hazard.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. Avicenna describes colic from litharge, but no one applies it. Lead white is face paint and pigment; lead glazes, pewter and lead-sweetened wine are everyday. Vitruvius is barely read. Local: potters; painters' workshops; apothecaries (biacca).
- **Soldering, brazing and tinning** [`soldering_tinning`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/soldering_tinning.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Goldsmiths, plumbers and coppersmiths solder, braze with borax and tin copper pots. Tinned iron sheet is a rare German import.
- **Pottery, kilns and fired brick** [`fired_brick_ceramics`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/fired_brick_ceramics.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Brick, roof tile and terracotta are a major local industry. Tableware is 'archaic maiolica', tin-glazed and painted in green and brown. Local: Impruneta (brick, tile, terracotta); potters of Montelupo and Bacchereto.
- **Porcelain** [`porcelain`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/porcelain.md) — K1, use none, make very-hard, accept high. Marco Polo's book mentions it and a few pieces reach Italy as treasures. Nobody knows the clay, the stone or the kiln heat. Elsewhere: Jingdezhen (China), blue-and-white under the Yuan.
- **Glassmaking and glassblowing** [`glassmaking`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/glassmaking.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Tuscan glassmakers come from the Valdelsa and make beakers, flasks, urine glasses and apothecary ware. Fine work is bought from Murano. Local: glassmakers (bicchierai) of Gambassi and Montaione; Florentine glass shops. Elsewhere: Murano.
- **Colourless and optical glass (cristallo, lead crystal, plate)** [`clear_glass`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/clear_glass.md) — K2, use partial, make hard, accept high. Cristallo does not exist yet. Glass is greenish or decolourised with manganese; spectacle lenses are ground from the clearest glass or rock crystal. Purifying soda ash is the missing step. Local: spectacle makers of Florence and Pisa. Elsewhere: Venice, guild rules on spectacle lenses and rock-crystal workers.
- **Glass mirrors (tin amalgam and silvering)** [`glass_mirrors`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/glass_mirrors.md) — K2, use partial, make hard, accept high. Mirrors are polished metal or small convex glass backed with lead. Flat, clear, evenly backed plates are beyond any glasshouse. Elsewhere: Germany and Venice, small convex glass mirrors.
- **Hydraulic lime, Roman concrete and Portland cement** [`hydraulic_cement`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/hydraulic_cement.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Masons line cisterns and found bridge piers with lime and crushed brick. Vitruvius on pozzolana survives in rare manuscripts. Burning true cement clinker is hard. Local: builders of the new Ponte Vecchio (1345); Opera del Duomo (campanile works). Elsewhere: Bay of Naples and Lazio, pozzolana.
- **Reinforced concrete** [`reinforced_concrete`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/reinforced_concrete.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. Iron tie rods across vaults and arches are familiar. Iron is hand-forged and dear; Roman-style concrete without iron is the realistic step.
- **Papermaking** [`paper`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/paper.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Rag paper serves merchants' ledgers, letters and notaries; books of standing are on parchment. Every copy is written by hand. Rags are the bottleneck. Local: Fabriano (watermarked paper); paper mills of Colle di Val d'Elsa; cartolai (stationers) of Florence.
- **Preparing textile fibres (wool, flax, cotton, silk)** [`textile_fibres`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/textile_fibres.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Villani counts over 200 wool workshops feeding some 30,000 people, working fine English wool. Raw wool, cloth and rags move through every quarter of the city. Local: Arte della Lana; Arte di Calimala (finishing of imported cloth); fulling mills on the Arno. Elsewhere: England, the best wool; Flanders, rival cloth towns.
- **Tanning leather** [`leather_tanning`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/leather_tanning.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Tanners work by the Arno with oak bark, myrtle and sumac; alum-tawed white leather too. A stinking trade, blamed for corrupting the air in plague time. Local: tanners by the Arno; Arte dei Cuoiai e Galigai.
- **Aluminium** [`aluminium`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/aluminium.md) — K0, use none, make impossible, accept medium. Alum is traded by the shipload, but nobody suspects a metal in it.
- **Wood tar and pitch** [`wood_tar_pitch`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/wood_tar_pitch.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Pitch seals casks, roofs and boats; Pisa and Genoa use it for galleys. Burning pitch and resin is a trusted way to cleanse plague air. Local: Casentino and Apennine forests; Maremma woods.
